constitution.title: Constitution of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar (2008)
constitution.publisher: Ministry of Information, Printing and Publishing Enterprise
constitution.note: Official English text printed by the Ministry of Information in September 2008, read in the 2015 revision as the Comparative Constitutions Project reproduces it, since the Union Election Commission and Hluttaw hosts refused this session. Art. 49: seven Regions, seven States, and the Union territories; art. 56: the five Self-Administered Zones and one Self-Administered Division; art. 60: the President is elected by the Presidential Electoral College of the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw's three groups; art. 109: the Pyithu Hluttaw has at most 330 representatives elected on the basis of townships and 110 Defence Services personnel nominated by the Commander-in-Chief; arts. 119, 151, and 168: five-year terms; art. 141: 168 elected Amyotha Hluttaw representatives, 12 from each Region or State, and 56 nominated Defence Services personnel; art. 161: two Region or State Hluttaw representatives from each township, one for each national race of at least 0.1 percent of the Union's population that has no Region, State, or Self-Administered Area of its own, and one third nominated Defence Services personnel; art. 276: Leading Bodies of Self-Administered Areas formed from Region or State Hluttaw representatives and nominees; art. 289: ward and village-tract administration assigned by law to a person respected by the community; art. 399: the Union Election Commission; art. 436: amendments to entrenched sections need a nation-wide referendum; art. 441: the Constitution was adopted by nation-wide referendum.

uec_constituencies.title: UEC announces constituencies for 2025 general election
uec_constituencies.publisher: The Global New Light of Myanmar (Ministry of Information)
uec_constituencies.note: Reports the Union Election Commission's Notifications 50/2025 (Pyithu Hluttaw), 51/2025 (Amyotha Hluttaw), 52/2025 (Region and State Hluttaws), and 53/2025 (Region and State Hluttaw ethnic constituencies) of 15 August 2025: 330 FPTP Pyithu Hluttaw constituencies; 84 FPTP and 26 PR Amyotha Hluttaw constituencies; 322 FPTP and 42 PR Region and State Hluttaw constituencies; 29 ethnic constituencies.

uec_votes_2026.title: UEC announces secured votes of political parties
uec_votes_2026.publisher: The Global New Light of Myanmar (Ministry of Information)
uec_votes_2026.note: Reports Union Election Commission announcement 34/2026 of 9 February 2026: the election held in phases from 28 December 2025 in 263 Pyithu Hluttaw, 99 Amyotha Hluttaw, 297 Region or State Hluttaw, and 29 ethnic constituencies; the Commission announced each candidate's votes and percentage and each party's seats.

ndsc_briefing.title: NDSC Information Team Leader briefs public on upcoming multiparty democratic election
ndsc_briefing.publisher: The Global New Light of Myanmar (Ministry of Information)
ndsc_briefing.note: Official briefing of November 2025 with the government's count of Myanmar's elections: Legislative Council elections under dyarchy on 11 November 1922, the first; six elections from 1922 to 1947, three in the parliamentary period (1948-1962), four under the Burma Socialist Programme Party (1962-1988), one under the SLORC and SPDC (1988-2010), and six since 2010 (general elections on 7 November 2010, 8 November 2015, and 8 November 2020, and three by-elections); FPTP for the Pyithu Hluttaw and a mixed-member proportional system for the Amyotha Hluttaw and the State and Region Hluttaws in 2025.

president_2026.title: Misinformation vs. Reality: The Truth Behind the 2026 General Election and Presidential Appointment
president_2026.publisher: The Global New Light of Myanmar (Ministry of Information)
president_2026.note: The President was elected by the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw by secret ballot on the morning of 3 April 2026 from the nominees of the Pyithu Hluttaw, Amyotha Hluttaw, and Defence Services representatives' groups (584 of 586 representatives attending); turnout in the 2025 general election was 13.14 million of 24.22 million eligible voters (54.22 percent).

classes.finest_note: Candidates' votes by constituency (one per township) in the Commission's announcements; the 2017 by-elections also by constituency on the open results portal
classes.note: At most 330 representatives elected on the basis of townships, plus 110 Defence Services personnel nominated by the Commander-in-Chief (Constitution art. 109); five-year term from the first session (art. 119). Single-member constituencies by first past the post in 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025. The Commission annulled the 2020 results in July 2021. The 2025 election was held in three phases (28 December 2025, 11 January 2026, and 25 January 2026) in 263 of the 330 constituencies. By-elections fill vacated seats: 1 April 2012, 1 April 2017 (loaded by mm.uec), and 3 November 2018.

classes.finest_note: The 2008 results were announced nationally and by Region and State in the state press; no township table has been found
classes.note: The 2008 Constitution was adopted by a nation-wide referendum (art. 441), held on 10 May 2008 and on 24 May 2008 in the townships hit by Cyclone Nargis; the 1974 Constitution was adopted by the referendum of December 1973. An amendment to the entrenched sections listed in art. 436(a) needs more than 75 percent of the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw and then a referendum carried by more than half of those eligible to vote; none has been held.

Mandalay, Nay Pyi Taw, and the municipal development affairs committees of the other Regions and States are formed under their own Region or State laws.

classes.name: ဥပဒေပြုကောင်စီ ရွေးကောက်ပွဲ
classes.name_en: Burma Legislative Council (dyarchy, 1922-1936), abolished
classes.note: Elected under the dyarchy of the Government of India Act as applied to Burma; the official count of six elections from 1922 to 1947 covers the Council elections of 1922, 1925, 1928, and 1932, the 1936 House of Representatives, and the 1947 Constituent Assembly. Results were printed in the colonial government's gazette and reports.

dates.quote: Under the Diarchy system, elections for the Legislative Council were held on 11 November 1922. Historical records show that this was the first election in the history of Myanmar.

dates.note: Council elections of 1925, 1928, and 1932, the second to fourth of the six the official briefing counts from 1922 to 1947.

classes.name: ပြည်သူ့လွှတ်တော် (၁၉၃၆) ရွေးကောက်ပွဲ
classes.name_en: House of Representatives of British Burma (1936 election), abolished
classes.note: Lower house under the Government of Burma Act 1935, which separated Burma from India from 1 April 1937; elected in 1936 and sitting until the Japanese occupation. The Senate was half elected by the House and half nominated. The fifth of the six elections the official briefing counts from 1922 to 1947.

dates.note: General election to the House of Representatives.

classes.name: တိုင်းပြုပြည်ပြုလွှတ်တော် ရွေးကောက်ပွဲ
classes.name_en: Constituent Assembly (1947), abolished
classes.note: Elected on 9 April 1947 to draft the 1947 Constitution of the Union of Burma, then served as the provisional parliament until 1951-52; the last of the six elections the official briefing counts from 1922 to 1947.

dates.note: Constituent Assembly election.

classes.name: ပြည်သူ့လွှတ်တော် (၁၉၄၇ ဖွဲ့စည်းပုံ) ရွေးကောက်ပွဲ
classes.name_en: Chamber of Deputies of the Union of Burma (1951-1962), abolished
classes.note: Lower house under the 1947 Constitution, elected by first past the post; the official briefing counts three elections in the parliamentary period (1951-52, held in phases from June 1951 to April 1952; 1956; and 1960). Dissolved by the coup of 2 March 1962.

dates.note: First parliamentary general election, held in phases from June 1951 to April 1952.
Second parliamentary general election.
Third parliamentary general election.

classes.name_en: Chamber of Nationalities of the Union of Burma (1951-1962), abolished
classes.note: Upper house under the 1947 Constitution with seats reserved for the states and nationalities; elected with the Chamber of Deputies in 1951-52, 1956, and 1960, some members chosen by state councils.

dates.note: Elected with the Chamber of Deputies in 1951-52, 1956, and 1960.

classes.note: Unicameral legislature under the 1974 Constitution, elected from single-party lists of the Burma Socialist Programme Party; the official briefing counts four elections in the BSPP period (1974, 1978, 1981, and 1985). Ended by the military takeover of 18 September 1988.

classes.name_en: People's Councils of states and divisions, townships, and wards and village tracts (1974-1988), abolished
classes.note: Under the 1974 Constitution, People's Councils at the state or division, township, and ward or village-tract levels were elected with the People's Assembly from single-party lists; abolished in 1988.

dates.note: Elected with the People's Assembly in 1974, 1978, 1981, and 1985.

classes.name: ပါတီစုံဒီမိုကရေစီ အထွေထွေရွေးကောက်ပွဲ (၁၉၉၀)
classes.name_en: Multiparty general election of 1990 (Pyithu Hluttaw), abolished
classes.note: Held on 27 May 1990 under the State Law and Order Restoration Council in single-member constituencies by first past the post; the assembly was never convened. The one election the official briefing counts for 1988-2010.

dates.note: Multiparty general election; results by constituency were announced by the election commission of the time in the state press.

classes.name: နိုင်ငံတော်သမ္မတ ရွေးချယ်ခြင်း
classes.name_en: President and Vice-Presidents, elected by the Presidential Electoral College
classes.note: The President is elected by the Presidential Electoral College, whose three groups (the elected Pyithu Hluttaw members, the elected Amyotha Hluttaw members, and the Defence Services representatives) each nominate a Vice-President; the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw then votes among the three (Constitution art. 60). Last held on 3 April 2026.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the members of the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw, not by a popular vote.

classes.name: တိုင်းဒေသကြီး သို့မဟုတ် ပြည်နယ် ဝန်ကြီးချုပ်
classes.name_en: Chief Ministers of the Regions and States
classes.note: The President selects a Region or State Hluttaw representative as Chief Minister and submits the name to the Hluttaw for approval (Constitution art. 261).
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the President with the Hluttaw's approval; there is no popular vote.

classes.name: ကိုယ်ပိုင်အုပ်ချုပ်ခွင့်ရ တိုင်း သို့မဟုတ် ဒေသ ဦးစီးအဖွဲ့
classes.name_en: Leading Bodies of the Self-Administered Division and Zones
classes.note: Each Leading Body is formed from the Region or State Hluttaw representatives elected from its townships, Defence Services representatives, and members they select, and chooses its Chairperson from among the elected representatives (Constitution art. 276).
classes.disposition_reason: Formed from members already elected to the Region or State Hluttaw, nominees, and co-opted members; no separate vote.

classes.name: ရပ်ကွက် သို့မဟုတ် ကျေးရွာအုပ်စု အုပ်ချုပ်ရေးမှူး
classes.name_en: Ward and village-tract administrators
classes.note: Ward and village-tract administration is assigned by law to a person respected by the community (Constitution art. 289); under the Ward or Village Tract Administration Law the administrator is chosen by the heads of ten-household groups, who are themselves chosen by the households, and confirmed by the township administrator.
classes.disposition_reason: An indirect selection by household representatives run by the General Administration Department, with no published votes.

classes.name: တပ်မတော်သား လွှတ်တော်ကိုယ်စားလှယ်
classes.name_en: Defence Services representatives in the Pyithu, Amyotha, and Region or State Hluttaws
classes.note: A quarter of the Union Hluttaw seats and a third of each Region or State Hluttaw's seats are held by Defence Services personnel nominated by the Commander-in-Chief (Constitution arts. 109(b), 141(b), and 161(d)).
classes.disposition_reason: Nominated by the Commander-in-Chief of the Defence Services; there is no vote.

classes.name: တရားသူကြီးများ
classes.name_en: Judges of the Supreme Court of the Union and the High Courts
classes.note: The Chief Justice and judges of the Supreme Court are nominated by the President and approved by the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw; High Court judges by the Chief Minister with the Region or State Hluttaw (Constitution arts. 299 and 308).
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are nominated and approved, never elected.

classes.name: ပါတီ ကိုယ်စားလှယ်လောင်း ရွေးချယ်ခြင်း
classes.name_en: Party candidate selection
classes.note: Parties registered under the Political Parties Registration Law nominate their own candidates; the Union Election Commission runs no primary or nominating contest.
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run nominating contest exists; parties pick candidates internally.
